name: example-web
description:
A small office LAN: **gw** connects it to the internet and forwards web requests from outside to the web server on **pc1**.

| Container | Address on LAN `10.0.10.0/24` (switch *lan*) |
|---|---|
| gw | `10.0.10.1` |
| pc1 (web server) | `10.0.10.10` |
| pc2 | `10.0.10.20` |

## Try it
1. **Deploy**, then open a console on pc2 and run:
   ```
   curl http://10.0.10.10
   ```
2. From your PC's browser, open `http://<Docker host>:8080` (click gw: the *Port mappings* section has the link). The request reaches gw, which forwards it to pc1.
3. From pc2, go out through gw's NAT:
   ```
   ping -c 3 1.1.1.1
   curl -I https://example.com
   ```
4. Capture the **gw–lan** cable while loading the page from your PC: the destination is `10.0.10.10`, not gw. On gw, see the NAT rules counting packets:
   ```
   iptables -t nat -L -n -v
   ```

## Questions
- [ ] Why does the web page answer on port 8080 of the Docker host, but port 80 on pc1?
- [ ] What address does pc1 see the browser's requests coming from? Why isn't it gw's?
- [ ] Remove the default route on pc1 (`ip route del default`). Which tests still work, and why?

nodes.name: gw
nodes.startup:
# Outbound: masquerade the LAN behind gw's nat0 address
nat-on

# Inbound (port forwarding): Docker publishes the host's port 8080 to gw's port 80 on nat0;
# send those requests on to the web server on pc1
iptables -t nat -C PREROUTING -i nat0 -p tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.0.10.10:80 2>/dev/null \
  || iptables -t nat -A PREROUTING -i nat0 -p tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.0.10.10:80

nodes.name: pc1
nodes.startup:
# gw is the way out of the LAN ip route replace default via 10.0.10.1 echo nameserver 1.1.1.1 > /etc/resolv.conf # The web page, then the web server (BusyBox httpd on port 80, serving /var/www) cat > /var/www/index.html < pc1

Hello from $(hostname)

Served by BusyBox httpd at 10.0.10.10, inside the DockerLab LAN.

HTML pkill -x httpd 2>/dev/null; busybox-extras httpd -p 80 -h /var/www

nodes.name: pc2
nodes.startup:
# gw is the way out of the LAN
ip route replace default via 10.0.10.1
echo nameserver 1.1.1.1 > /etc/resolv.conf

notes.text:
From your PC: http://<Docker host>:8080
Docker host :8080 → gw:80 (nat0)
→ DNAT → pc1 10.0.10.10:80

images.dockerlab/router:latest:
FROM alpine:latest

# Networking tools for a gateway or router
RUN apk add --no-cache iproute2 iptables tcpdump bind-tools curl iputils

# nat-on: masquerade traffic leaving through the NAT interface (nat0).
# Safe to run more than once; use it in startup commands.
RUN printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/sh' \
      'iptables -t nat -C POSTROUTING -o nat0 -j MASQUERADE 2>/dev/null || iptables -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o nat0 -j MASQUERADE' \
      > /usr/local/bin/nat-on && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/nat-on
images.dockerlab/host:latest:
FROM alpine:latest

# Everyday tools for an end host: full ip, packet capture, DNS lookups, web requests
RUN apk add --no-cache iproute2 tcpdump bind-tools curl iputils
images.dockerlab/web:latest:
FROM alpine:latest

# A small web server (BusyBox httpd), plus the end-host tools: full ip, packet capture, DNS lookups, web requests
RUN apk add --no-cache busybox-extras iproute2 tcpdump bind-tools curl iputils
RUN mkdir -p /var/www
